questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The most determining factor for choosing McMaster was the prospects of enrolling in Virology courses and learning more about Immunology. The second key factor was the nature that aligned with my ambitions of travelling in Canada. Another important influence was my colleague at CBMR who recommended that I chose a destination far away from Denmark to gain a new and diverse perspective on academics, which was different from the Danish approach.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Prior to my arrival I had arranged an airport pick-up by my landlord. I know other students who used the campus shuttlebus going directly to campus. Offers like these was sent out pr email in advance, so all the exchange students where informed. McMaster also arranged tutors in the airport as a welcome. McMaster succeded in sending out all these improtant informationsn through multiple media channels, most arrival information was sent out pr. Email and the same infromation was likewise posted on the schools social media channels. Arrival was also a theme in the webinar series.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Welcome orientations on campus during the first weeks of the semester. These orientations was tailored to the exchange students providing us with a lot of relevant information about the city of Hamilton, and the University history and academic structure. The unaswered questions from these orientations was easialy answered by the respective offices pr. Email. I remember asking further into course selection. Besides the academic questions the university also provides helpful ressources regarding housing, phone bills, and banking specific questions and scholarships. My situation was different since, I moved in with a lanldord, who provided me with a lot of information regarding SIM cards, bank accounts, and rental payment in Canada.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very, easy if you are out in advance prior to your arrival in Canada. The university provides resources to ensure every student find housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Avoid downtown Hamilton, it is further from main campus and less cozy. Instead turn your eyes towards Dundass or Westdale. These areas are much more welcoming to students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is a huge difference between on-campus housing and off-campus housing. The main difference is the prize and the size of accomodation. Usually there is more roommates on-campus and less off-campus. However the prize difference favours on-campus residence. The university, in my opinion, does not put a lot of trust in you as a tennant, as refelcted by the contract your must sign. And for that reason I recommend finding a place off-campus. Especially in Dundass or Westdale, both parts of the city is close to campus, reasonable prized and not too loud throughout the semester. Finding accomodation is made easier through the partner website ”PlacesForStudents”. Very intuitive and useful in the search for residence. More precise links are provided by the university during the webinars on housing.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Enrolling in courses is done through the Mosaic platform online by searching for the specific course code. McMaster operates with the rule, that the majority of courses a student is enrolled in must be from within the faculty, the student is assigned to. This rule can be bend, allowing you to enroll in more courses from a different faculty ie. Health Sciences instead of Science. In my situation I enrolled in two HTHSCI courses while bieng assigned to the Science Faculty. Once the specific course is identified the course is added to the basket on mosaic. From here its now a question of clicking enroll. If all prerequisites are met and seats are available you will be enrolled in the course. If the prerequisites does not match, you can always email the professor or the office of registry at the specific faculty. Mosaic in general has a user friendly interface where you can add and drop courses as you like, during the regristration period and the ”add&drop” window in the beginning of the semester.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Reminders sent out pr email, by the exchange coordinator at McMaster. In the months before depature to Canada, the exchange office will host a webinar on course regristration and answer questions reagarding elligibilltiy and prerequisites. Also the iCent app is very usefull in navigating your questions. Sometimes you'll find answers to course registration or at least the people you should email with the questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I followed the recommendations and signed up for my courses early in the registration period. This helped me secure my seat in the classes I had prioritised the most.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
You do not have to enroll in 5 courses as a KU student - 4 is enough. There is some discrepencies in what constitutes a fulltime student at McMaster, sometimes 3 courses is considered full course load, in other cases student must enroll in 5 courses.
Use Reddit Course title + course code. And in most cases you'll find a review of course content, group work, grading and the professor and TA (teaching assistants).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Level 3 courses are overall a bit easier compared to 8 weeks of course material at KU. Where as the level 4 courses is more similar to the KU level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Huge difference, group work played a larger role in my Immunology and Epidemiology courses. Whereas my course in Biochemical Pharmacology is more similar to a KU, with most of the content being covered in lectures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Principles of Virology, Introductory Immunology, Introduction to Epidemiology and Biochemical Pharmacology.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Principles of Virology is my first recommendation, to anyon with the ambition of pursuing virology later on in their studies. Dr. Muularcky is a highly passionate professor with many great skills in teaching.
The other course I highly reccomend is the Immunology course, where Dr. Koeing uses many great analogies and real worl examples to explian the complicated concepts in immunology.
The last course I reccommend is the Epidemiology, where Dr. Pritchard gives a very detailed introduction to the field of epidemiology and the tools used in this field of research.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Prevent your computer from crashing while being abroad, by investing in one while being in Denmark. One of my friends was cutting it very close with her computer. 
I did experience an unexpected transfer fee, when I moved my Canadian telephone number between to phone companies. This was neccessary inorder to have the abilltiy to call my danish bank.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Eggs, sliced cheese where more expensive
Coffee and snacks at a caffee was less expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A broad selection of societies and clubs were available to exchange students at McMaster. A few examples would be the book club, the Outdoor Club, the Taylor Swift Society, Black Student Society, Astronomy society, The Climbing club.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The outdoor club, the trips they arrange takes you to some pretty impressive and beutiful destinations, such as Alqonquin National Park.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Short trips, waterfall hike around the Niagra Escarpment near Hamilton. Visit Niagra Falls and the town Niagra On the Lake
Longer Trips, visit Toronto, Montreal, Ottowa

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The canadian culturen is very similar to the western culture in Denmark, so in large parts adjusting was not that difficult. They do how ever emphasize the Indiginous population by saying a land acknowledgement. These are more prominent in the webinars and the beginning of the term.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Use the opportunity through gruop work to socialize with Canadian students, it takes some effort to arrange something but it is worth it.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The entire campus has different programs spanning from humanities to engeneering and to STEM. Everyone is on the same campus, so you're likely to meet someone outside of your own program.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The overall welcomming spirit on campus. I would say Canadian univerosties is quiet similar in terms of inclusion and openess towards new cultures.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Bring a danish extension cord – that is a life saver, Excpect the course load to be easier on a weekly basis, however a bit challenging over the full semester.
Maximize the time you spend travelling and explore Canada while you're over there.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The on campus food is reasonably priced. In general professors and local students find it vluable to have an exchange student in the class room.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Networking woth people in Canada. Such that I have contacts I can reach out to, the next time I am travelling. Getting to know other students from abroad in a similar situation as myself.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Balancing the academic work and the travelling with friends.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: If you have any doubts regarding the decision of going/not going. I highly recommend going abroad! I am grateful for the friendships and people I got know along the way, during my semester at McMaster University.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
